findings.source_quote: ὡς τὸν γέροντα ζητεῖν μέλλων παρ’ αὐτοῖς
findings.english_quote: that he was going to demand the old man from them
findings.issue: παρ’ αὐτοῖς has the dative, expressing location or association: seeking the old man among them, at their place, or in their keeping. The contextual rendering “demand” is defensible, but the note describes only alternatives involving information, an accounting, or a demand “from them”; it does not preserve the direct locative reading. The disclosure therefore inadequately represents the supplied construction.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare “that he was going to look for the old man among them” with the contextual demand rendering. Either adopt the source-transparent locative wording, or retain “demand” with a corrected note explaining the dative, preserving the locative alternative, and explaining why seeking someone in their keeping is construed as demanding him from them. Any revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἐνίους δὲ καὶ χαλεπαίνοντας αὐτῷ ὡς Σίμωνι διὰ τὴν πρὸς Πέτρον ὑπερβάλλουσαν στοργὴν
findings.english_quote: some, angry with him as though he were Simon because of his surpassing affection for Peter
findings.issue: “His” assigns the affection to the man taken for Simon. The Greek supplies no possessive with στοργὴν, and the surrounding account most naturally makes the townspeople’s exceptional affection for Peter the reason for their anger against the supposed Simon. The draft thus introduces an inadequately supported attribution that changes the represented motive. Its note discusses the affection’s intensity but neither discloses this referent choice nor preserves the contextual alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “some, angry with him as though he were Simon because of the surpassing affection for Peter,” with a note explaining that the possessor is unexpressed and that the townspeople’s affection is the most natural contextual reading. Alternatively, propose “their surpassing affection for Peter” with that same disclosure and rationale. The replacement must undergo fresh review.
